rationale: llubenchmark is a tiny (191 lines, 4 functions), allocation-heavy linked-list benchmark whose hot loop makes runtime overhead the binding constraint, so all RuntimeCost weights are kept low (0.2-0.4) to discourage applying expensive transformations to the hot path, while SecurityGain and DiversityGain are weighted high so feature-matched cold/sensitive regions still get meaningful protection. SUB is favored most (near-zero risk, cheap, strong strength-reduction resistance) and FLA/BCF are next as the primary control-flow deterrents, with FLA's CorrectnessRisk held at 0.3 since flattening a compact main with loop-carried list pointers is the most correctness-sensitive transform here. SPLIT and IBR get moderate weights as cheap, composable diversifiers that harden FLA's flattened dispatcher, while ICALL (0.3 correctness risk, indirect-call dispatch can perturb the allocate/main call pattern) and IGV (few globals to hide in such a small program, limited payoff) are kept as low-weight options so they apply only where features strongly favor them.
